title: Haematology, coagulation and transfusion
summary: Haematology for the ICU: restrictive transfusion and reactions, anticoagulant reversal, DIC and sepsis-induced coagulopathy, HIT, TTP/TMA, and ICU thrombocytopenia with viscoelastic-guided therapy.

topics.title: Red cell, platelet and plasma transfusion; reactions
topics.summary: Restrictive thresholds (AABB 2023), platelet and plasma indications, and recognising transfusion reactions (TACO, TRALI, haemolysis).

definition.text: Restrictive transfusion is safe for most critically ill adults: transfuse red cells at Hb < 7 g/dL; higher thresholds for specific groups.

steps.title: Red cells
steps.detail: Hb < 7 g/dL for hospitalised and ICU patients including septic shock; < 7.5 for cardiac surgery; < 8 for orthopaedic surgery or pre-existing cardiovascular disease. Give 1 unit, then reassess.

steps.title: Acute MI
steps.detail: MINT suggested a possible benefit of a liberal (Hb < 10) strategy in MI with anaemia; consider a higher threshold.

steps.title: Platelets
steps.detail: Prophylactic < 10 × 10⁹/L (hypoproliferative); < 20 for CVC insertion; < 50 for LP or major non-neuraxial surgery; < 100 for neurosurgery/eye surgery or ICH; > 50 in active bleeding.

steps.title: Plasma
steps.detail: Not for isolated raised INR without bleeding or before low-risk procedures; 15-20 mL/kg for bleeding with factor deficiency.

steps.title: Massive haemorrhage
steps.detail: Use the massive transfusion protocol with balanced ratios (see trauma module); monitor Ca²⁺, temperature and viscoelastic tests.

steps.title: Bedside safety
steps.detail: Two-person ID check, baseline obs; observe first 15 min closely; stop transfusion at first sign of a reaction.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg with Hb 6.4: 1 unit over 2-3 h → expected Hb ~7.4 g/dL
70 kg: 1 SDP or 6 RDP; check 1-h post-count

tables.title: Acute transfusion reactions
rows: Stop, exclude haemolysis/sepsis, paracetamol; may restart
Stop; antihistamine; adrenaline 0.5 mg IM for anaphylaxis
Fever, loin pain, hypotension, haemoglobinuria, DIC
Stop, keep line open, fluids, recheck ID, DAT, haemolysis screen, inform blood bank
Dyspnoea, hypertension, raised JVP, pulmonary oedema within 12 h
Hypoxaemia, bilateral infiltrates within 6 h, often hypotension, no volume overload
Stop, supportive (lung-protective ventilation), avoid diuretics, report donor
Stop, culture bag and patient, broad-spectrum antibiotics

redFlags.text: Fever, hypotension and loin pain within minutes of starting blood: suspect ABO incompatibility - stop immediately.

pitfalls.text: Transfusing 2 units reflexively in stable patients: give single units and reassess.
Giving FFP to correct mildly raised INR before a central line.

pearls.text: TACO is the commonest cause of transfusion-related death in many haemovigilance systems; watch fluid balance in elderly and cardiac patients.

nodes.text: Hb below threshold (7; 7.5 cardiac surgery; 8 CVD/ortho)?
Do not transfuse; treat cause (iron, B12, bleeding)

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Oxygen delivery is maintained at Hb 7 g/dL in most patients by increased cardiac output and extraction. Stored red cells have storage lesions, and transfusion carries immunomodulatory, infectious and volume risks.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- AABB 2023 international guideline: restrictive thresholds for most patients [Carson 2023].
- TRISS: Hb 7 vs 9 in septic shock - similar mortality with half the transfusions [Holst 2014].
- MINT (3,504 patients with MI): liberal strategy did not significantly reduce death/MI (16.9% vs 14.5%) but the direction favoured liberal [Carson 2023 MINT].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Thresholds in acute brain injury (TRAIN trial suggested benefit of liberal) and in MI.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- India relies on voluntary and replacement donation; blood components (PRBC, SDP, cryo) availability varies by district. NAT testing is not universal; transfusion-transmitted infection risk is higher than in high-income countries, reinforcing restrictive use.
- Haemovigilance Programme of India (IPC/NIB) accepts reports of adverse reactions.

topics.title: Anticoagulant and antiplatelet reversal
topics.summary: Agent-specific reversal for warfarin, dabigatran, factor Xa inhibitors, heparin/LMWH and antiplatelets in major bleeding.

definition.text: Major bleeding = haemodynamic instability, bleeding at a critical site (intracranial, spinal, pericardial, airway, retroperitoneal, intra-ocular), or Hb drop ≥ 2 g/dL / ≥ 2 units needed. Reverse anticoagulation for major bleeding or emergency surgery.

steps.title: Assess
steps.detail: Site and severity, last dose time, renal function, INR/aPTT/anti-Xa/TT. General measures: compression, source control, transfusion, stop antithrombotics.

steps.title: Warfarin
steps.detail: Vitamin K 5-10 mg IV + 4F-PCC (INR-based 25-50 units/kg, or fixed 1,000-1,500 units); recheck INR 30 min after. FFP 15-20 mL/kg only if PCC unavailable.

steps.title: Dabigatran
steps.detail: Idarucizumab 5 g IV; if unavailable, PCC 50 units/kg; haemodialysis removes dabigatran.

steps.title: Rivaroxaban/apixaban
steps.detail: Andexanet alfa where available; otherwise 4F-PCC 50 units/kg (or 2,000 units). Activated charcoal if ingested within 2-4 h.

steps.title: Heparin/LMWH
steps.detail: Protamine 1 mg per 100 units UFH given in last 2-3 h (max 50 mg); enoxaparin 1 mg per mg (≤ 8 h) or 0.5 mg per mg (8-12 h).

steps.title: Antiplatelets
steps.detail: Platelet transfusion not recommended for antiplatelet-associated ICH (PATCH: worse outcome) unless emergency neurosurgery; consider desmopressin 0.3 mcg/kg.

steps.title: Thrombolytic-associated bleeding
steps.detail: Cryoprecipitate to fibrinogen > 150 mg/dL and tranexamic acid.

steps.title: Restart plan
steps.detail: Decide when to restart anticoagulation (often 7-14 days after ICH, 1-3 days after GI bleed control) with the specialist team.

doseCards.dose: 1 mg per 100 units UFH in last 2-3 h (max 50 mg)
doseCards.workedExample: Infusion 1,000 units/h: about 2,500 units in last 2.5 h → 25 mg protamine over 10 min
70 kg: 21 mcg in 50 mL NS over 30 min

redFlags.text: Intracranial haemorrhage on any anticoagulant: reverse immediately, do not wait for coagulation results.

pitfalls.text: Giving PCC without vitamin K for warfarin: INR rebounds after 6-8 h.
Transfusing platelets for antiplatelet-associated ICH without surgery.

pearls.text: Normal thrombin time essentially excludes significant dabigatran effect.

nodes.text: Stop drug, local control, transfuse, labs
Protamine per dose in last 2-3 h
Supportive; desmopressin; platelets only if surgery

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Warfarin depletes vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, X (PCC replaces them immediately; vitamin K restores synthesis over 6-24 h). DOACs directly inhibit thrombin or factor Xa; reversal requires antidotes or overwhelming the inhibition with factor concentrates.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ACC 2020 ECDP on bleeding with oral anticoagulants [Tomaselli 2020].
- PATCH: platelet transfusion increased death or dependence in antiplatelet-associated ICH (OR 2.05) [Baharoglu 2016].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Andexanet thrombosis risk and cost; PCC for DOACs is off-label with limited evidence.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Andexanet is not available in India and idarucizumab is expensive; 4F-PCC (or FFP if unavailable) is the practical option.
- Acenocoumarol (more commonly used than warfarin in India) is reversed the same way.

quiz.stem: Warfarin ICH, INR 4.5, 80 kg. Best reversal:
Protamine for UFH infusion 1,200 units/h (last 2 h ≈ 2,400 units):

topics.title: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
topics.summary: Score DIC (ISTH) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy, treat the cause, and give products only for bleeding or procedures.

definition.text: DIC is an acquired syndrome of systemic intravascular coagulation activation causing microvascular thrombosis and consumption of platelets and factors. Causes: sepsis, trauma, obstetric (abruption, AFE), malignancy (APML), severe pancreatitis, snakebite (venom-induced consumption coagulopathy in India).

steps.title: Score
steps.detail: ISTH overt DIC score ≥ 5 (platelets, D-dimer, PT, fibrinogen); in sepsis, SIC score ≥ 4 identifies earlier coagulopathy. Repeat daily: trends matter.

steps.title: Treat the cause
steps.detail: Source control and antibiotics in sepsis; delivery in obstetric DIC; ATRA for APML; antivenom for snakebite coagulopathy.

steps.title: Bleeding or procedure
steps.detail: Platelets if < 50 × 10⁹/L and bleeding; FFP 15-30 mL/kg if PT/aPTT > 1.5× with bleeding; fibrinogen < 150 mg/dL with bleeding: cryoprecipitate.

steps.title: No bleeding
steps.detail: Platelets only if < 10-20 × 10⁹/L; do not give FFP for lab values alone.

steps.title: Thrombosis-predominant
steps.detail: Therapeutic heparin in DIC with thrombosis (e.g. purpura fulminans, solid tumour) if not bleeding; VTE prophylaxis in all non-bleeding DIC.

steps.title: Antifibrinolytics
steps.detail: Generally avoid TXA in sepsis-DIC; consider in hyperfibrinolytic DIC (APML, trauma, some obstetric).

tables.title: ISTH overt DIC score (with an underlying cause)
tables.caption: Score ≥ 5 = overt DIC (repeat daily); < 5 suggests non-overt DIC (repeat in 1-2 days). D-dimer cut-offs depend on local assay.

redFlags.text: Purpura fulminans (meningococcal sepsis): rapidly progressive skin necrosis with DIC - early antibiotics, products, consider protein C concentrate.

pitfalls.text: Treating DIC numbers with products in a non-bleeding patient.
Relying on a single normal fibrinogen: it is an acute-phase reactant and may fall only late in sepsis.

pearls.text: APML presents with profound hyperfibrinolytic DIC: start ATRA on suspicion and keep fibrinogen > 150 mg/dL and platelets > 30-50.

nodes.text: ISTH DIC score (SIC in sepsis); treat underlying cause
Platelets < 50; FFP 15-30 mL/kg; cryo if fibrinogen < 150
VTE prophylaxis; platelets only if < 10-20; repeat score daily
Reassess after products; continue cause-directed therapy

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Tissue factor expression on monocytes and endothelium drives thrombin generation, while anticoagulant pathways (antithrombin, protein C) and fibrinolysis (raised PAI-1 in sepsis) are suppressed, producing microthrombi and organ failure; consumption leads to bleeding.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ISTH DIC score (2001) and harmonised guidance (2013) [Taylor 2001; Wada 2013].
- SIC criteria identify patients with sepsis coagulopathy earlier than overt DIC [Iba 2017].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Anticoagulant therapy (antithrombin, thrombomodulin, heparin) in sepsis-induced coagulopathy: used in Japan, not recommended routinely elsewhere.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Snakebite (Russell's viper, saw-scaled viper) causes venom-induced consumption coagulopathy that responds to antivenom, not FFP; use the 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT).
- Falciparum malaria, dengue and leptospirosis are common Indian causes of DIC-like coagulopathy.

quiz.stem: Non-bleeding DIC with platelets 35 and INR 1.8:
quiz.explanation: Products only for bleeding/procedures or platelets < 10-20.

topics.title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
topics.summary: Use the 4Ts score, stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant when probability is intermediate or high, and confirm with PF4 and functional assays.

definition.text: HIT is an immune (anti-PF4/heparin IgG) prothrombotic disorder: platelet fall > 50% typically 5-10 days after heparin start (or within 24 h if exposed in the previous 30-100 days), with venous or arterial thrombosis in up to 50%.

steps.title: Calculate 4Ts
steps.detail: Low probability (≤ 3): HIT unlikely, do not test, continue heparin. Intermediate (4-5) or high (6-8): act.

steps.title: Stop all heparin
steps.detail: Including flushes, heparin-coated catheters and LMWH.

steps.title: Start non-heparin anticoagulant
steps.detail: Argatroban (critically ill, renal failure, may need procedures), bivalirudin, fondaparinux or a DOAC (stable patients) - at treatment doses even without thrombosis.

steps.title: Test
steps.detail: PF4/heparin immunoassay; if positive, functional assay (serotonin release or HIPA) to confirm.

steps.title: Look for thrombosis
steps.detail: Bilateral lower-limb compression ultrasound in all; upper limb if CVC.

steps.title: Avoid
steps.detail: Platelet transfusion (unless bleeding/high-risk procedure); warfarin until platelets recovered to ≥ 150 × 10⁹/L (warfarin necrosis, limb gangrene); give vitamin K if HIT diagnosed on warfarin.

steps.title: Duration
steps.detail: Without thrombosis (isolated HIT): until platelet recovery and up to 3 months; with thrombosis: 3 months.

doseCards.dose: 0.5-1.2 mcg/kg/min in organ failure (2 mcg/kg/min if no organ dysfunction)
doseCards.target: aPTT 1.5-3 × baseline (check 2 h after each change)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg at 1 mcg/kg/min = 70 mcg/min = 4.2 mg/h = 4.2 mL/h

tables.title: 4Ts score
rows: Day 5-10, or ≤ day 1 with heparin in past 30 days
Day > 10 or unclear; or ≤ day 1 with heparin 30-100 days ago
New proven thrombosis, skin necrosis, anaphylactoid reaction to IV heparin bolus
tables.caption: 0-3 low, 4-5 intermediate, 6-8 high probability.

redFlags.text: Limb ischaemia, new thrombosis or skin necrosis with falling platelets on heparin.

pitfalls.text: Ordering HIT antibodies for every thrombocytopenic ICU patient: a low 4Ts score has high negative predictive value; positive ELISA alone is common after surgery/CPB.
Stopping heparin without starting an alternative anticoagulant: thrombosis risk is high.

pearls.text: Sepsis-related thrombocytopenia in ICU is far more common than HIT, but post-cardiac surgery a second platelet fall after day 5 suggests HIT.

nodes.text: ≤ 3: HIT unlikely; continue heparin, find other cause
HIT confirmed: continue non-heparin anticoagulation 1-3 months
HIT excluded: resume heparin if needed

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: IgG antibodies against PF4-heparin complexes bind platelet FcγRIIa receptors, causing platelet activation, procoagulant microparticles and thrombin generation - hence thrombosis, not bleeding.
consultantNotes.evidence: - ASH 2018 HIT guideline [Cuker 2018]. 4Ts low score NPV ~99% [Lo 2006].
consultantNotes.controversies: - DOACs as first-line in stable HIT; management of HIT needing cardiac surgery.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Functional assays (SRA/HIPA) are rarely available in India; diagnosis relies on 4Ts plus PF4 ELISA (IgG-specific preferred) with a high optical density supporting HIT.
- Argatroban may not be stocked; fondaparinux and bivalirudin are alternatives.

topics.title: TTP and thrombotic microangiopathy
topics.summary: Recognise MAHA with thrombocytopenia, use PLASMIC, start urgent plasma exchange and immunosuppression, and distinguish HUS, DIC and pregnancy TMAs.

definition.text: TMA = microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia (schistocytes, raised LDH, low haptoglobin, negative DAT) + thrombocytopenia ± organ injury. Immune TTP: ADAMTS13 activity < 10% due to autoantibodies; untreated mortality ~90%.

steps.title: Confirm MAHA
steps.detail: Peripheral smear (schistocytes > 1%), LDH, haptoglobin, reticulocytes, bilirubin, DAT, coagulation (normal in TTP), creatinine, troponin. Send ADAMTS13 before plasma.

steps.title: PLASMIC score
steps.detail: Platelets < 30, haemolysis, no active cancer, no transplant, MCV < 90, INR < 1.5, creatinine < 2 mg/dL: 6-7 = high probability of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency.

steps.title: Urgent plasma exchange
steps.detail: If TTP suspected (PLASMIC high): start TPE (1-1.5 plasma volumes daily) within hours; if TPE delayed, give FFP 15-30 mL/kg meanwhile.

steps.title: Immunosuppression
steps.detail: Methylprednisolone 1 g/day × 3 (or prednisolone 1 mg/kg); rituximab 375 mg/m² weekly; caplacizumab where available.

steps.title: Avoid platelets
steps.detail: Platelet transfusion only for life-threatening bleeding; aspirin/LMWH prophylaxis once platelets > 50 × 10⁹/L.

steps.title: Consider differentials
steps.detail: STEC-HUS (bloody diarrhoea), atypical HUS (complement - eculizumab), DIC, HELLP/pre-eclampsia, malignant hypertension, scleroderma renal crisis, drugs (quinine, gemcitabine, calcineurin inhibitors), infections.

steps.title: Monitor response
steps.detail: Daily platelets and LDH; continue TPE until platelets > 150 × 10⁹/L for 2 days.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg: 1,050-2,100 mL; watch for volume overload

doseCards.dose: 10 mg IV before first TPE, then 10 mg SC daily

tables.title: TMA differential
rows: Very low platelets (< 30), mild AKI, neuro symptoms, ADAMTS13 < 10%
Pregnancy > 20 weeks or postpartum, hypertension, raised liver enzymes
Very high BP, retinopathy; improves with BP control

redFlags.text: Neurological symptoms, chest pain or raised troponin in TTP signal high mortality: urgent TPE and ICU.

pitfalls.text: Transfusing platelets in TTP: may precipitate thrombosis.
Waiting for ADAMTS13 results (days) before starting plasma exchange.

pearls.text: Normal coagulation tests with schistocytes and severe thrombocytopenia point to TTP rather than DIC.

nodes.text: Evaluate HUS/aHUS, HELLP, drugs, malignant HTN
Immune TTP: TPE, steroids, rituximab ± caplacizumab
Not TTP: stop TPE per haematology; aHUS → eculizumab

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Without ADAMTS13, ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers accumulate and spontaneously bind platelets in high-shear microvasculature, causing platelet-rich microthrombi (brain, heart, kidney) and red cell fragmentation.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ISTH 2020 TTP guidelines [Zheng 2020].
- PLASMIC score derivation/validation [Bendapudi 2017].
- HERCULES: caplacizumab reduced time to platelet normalisation and the composite of TTP death/recurrence/major thrombosis [Scully 2019].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Caplacizumab without TPE in selected patients; rituximab timing.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- ADAMTS13 testing is available only in a few Indian reference labs (results take days), so decisions rely on PLASMIC and smear.
- TPE availability is limited outside tertiary centres; FFP infusion is the bridge while arranging transfer.

options: High probability of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency

topics.title: ICU thrombocytopenia and viscoelastic testing
topics.summary: Systematic approach to low platelets in ICU and how to read TEG/ROTEM to target fibrinogen, plasma, platelets and antifibrinolytics.

definition.text: Thrombocytopenia (< 150 × 10⁹/L) affects 20-40% of ICU patients and independently predicts mortality. Viscoelastic tests (TEG, ROTEM) measure whole-blood clot formation, strength and lysis in 10-30 min.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.detail: Exclude pseudothrombocytopenia (EDTA clumping): repeat in citrate tube, check smear.

steps.title: Find the cause
steps.detail: Sepsis/DIC, dilution/massive transfusion, drugs (linezolid, vancomycin, piperacillin, valproate, heparin), HIT, TTP/TMA, liver disease/hypersplenism, ECMO/IABP/CRRT, marrow failure, tropical infections (dengue, malaria, leptospirosis, scrub typhus).

steps.title: Transfusion thresholds
steps.detail: Prophylactic < 10; < 20 for CVC; < 50 for LP/major surgery/active bleeding; < 100 for neurosurgery/ICH.

steps.title: Viscoelastic-guided bleeding management
steps.detail: Use TEG/ROTEM algorithms to target therapy rather than empirical ratios once initial resuscitation underway.

steps.title: Read the trace
steps.detail: Prolonged clotting time (R/CT): factor deficiency → plasma or PCC. Low clot amplitude with low FIBTEM/functional fibrinogen: fibrinogen (cryo/concentrate). Low amplitude with normal FIBTEM: platelets. Increased lysis (LY30/ML > 15%): tranexamic acid.

steps.title: Heparin effect
steps.detail: ROTEM INTEM vs HEPTEM (or TEG with heparinase) identifies residual heparin → protamine.

tables.title: ROTEM/TEG-guided therapy (typical triggers)
rows: EXTEM CT > 80 s / TEG R prolonged
FIBTEM A5 < 8-10 mm / low TEG functional fibrinogen
EXTEM A5 < 35 mm with normal FIBTEM / TEG MA low
tables.caption: Thresholds differ between devices and algorithms; use your unit's validated algorithm.

redFlags.text: Platelets falling > 50% after day 5 on heparin, or with haemolysis: think HIT or TTP.

pitfalls.text: Using one universal ROTEM threshold across different devices.

pearls.text: Linezolid-associated thrombocytopenia is common after 10-14 days, especially with renal impairment.

nodes.text: Sepsis/DIC, drugs, liver, dilution, infections, devices; transfuse by threshold

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: ICU thrombocytopenia arises from consumption (sepsis, DIC, devices), sequestration (hypersplenism), dilution, reduced production (marrow suppression, drugs) and immune destruction (HIT, drug-induced antibodies).
consultantNotes.evidence:
- ESAIC 2022/2023 guideline supports viscoelastic-guided bleeding management to reduce transfusion [Kietaibl 2023].
- AABB 2015 platelet thresholds [Kaufman 2015].
consultantNotes.controversies: - Prophylactic platelets before CVC in ultrasound-guided era (PACER trial suggests lower thresholds may be safe in experienced hands).
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Dengue, malaria, leptospirosis and scrub typhus are frequent causes of severe thrombocytopenia in Indian ICUs, especially during monsoon; prophylactic platelet transfusion in dengue without bleeding is not recommended by national guidelines (see tropical fevers module).
- Viscoelastic testing is limited to tertiary centres.

quiz.stem: FIBTEM A5 6 mm in a bleeding patient suggests:
First step for unexpected platelets 40 with no bleeding:
options: Check smear / citrate sample for clumping

drugs.name: Packed red blood cells
drugs.adultDose: 1 unit at a time in non-bleeding patients, then reassess Hb (each unit raises Hb ~1 g/dL in a 70 kg adult).
drugs.preparationIndia: Indian PRBC unit ~250-350 mL (from 350 or 450 mL donation).

drugs.name: Platelet concentrate
drugs.indications: Thrombocytopenia with bleeding or below prophylactic threshold
drugs.adultDose: 1 apheresis (single-donor) unit or 4-6 random-donor units (1 unit/10 kg); expected rise 30-50 × 10⁹/L per apheresis unit.
drugs.preparationIndia: Random-donor ~50-60 mL each; single-donor apheresis ~200-300 mL.

drugs.name: Fresh frozen plasma
drugs.indications: Bleeding with coagulation factor deficiency; TTP if plasma exchange delayed; warfarin reversal if PCC unavailable
drugs.adultDose: 15-20 mL/kg (about 4-5 units of ~200-250 mL in 70 kg).
drugs.cautions: TACO, TRALI, allergic reactions; slow to thaw (20-30 min).

drugs.name: Four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate
drugs.indications: Warfarin reversal in major bleeding; factor Xa inhibitor bleeding when andexanet unavailable
drugs.adultDose: Warfarin: INR 2-4 25 units/kg, 4-6 35 units/kg, > 6 50 units/kg (max 5,000 units), or fixed 1,000-1,500 units. Xa inhibitor: 50 units/kg (or 2,000 units).
drugs.preparationIndia: 500 or 600 unit vials (factor IX units); reconstitute with supplied water.
drugs.cautions: Thrombosis risk; always give with vitamin K for warfarin.
drugs.verify: Brand availability and cost in India; some hospitals stock only 3-factor PCC.

drugs.name: Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione)
drugs.adultDose: Major bleeding: 5-10 mg slow IV (with PCC). INR > 10 without bleeding: 2.5-5 mg oral.

drugs.name: Idarucizumab
drugs.indications: Dabigatran reversal for life-threatening bleeding or urgent surgery
drugs.verify: Availability in India limited and costly.

drugs.name: Protamine sulfate
drugs.adultDose: UFH: 1 mg per 100 units given in previous 2-3 h (max 50 mg). Enoxaparin: 1 mg per 1 mg enoxaparin if within 8 h (0.5 mg per mg if 8-12 h); partial reversal only.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension, anaphylaxis, pulmonary hypertension (fish allergy, prior protamine insulin, vasectomy).

drugs.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP)
drugs.indications: Antiplatelet-associated or uraemic platelet dysfunction with bleeding
drugs.adultDose: 0.3 mcg/kg IV in 50 mL NS over 30 min (single dose).
drugs.cautions: Hyponatraemia (restrict free water), tachyphylaxis after repeated doses.

drugs.name: Argatroban
drugs.adultDose: 2 mcg/kg/min IV (0.5-1.2 mcg/kg/min in heart failure, multi-organ failure, hepatic dysfunction or post-cardiac surgery); titrate to aPTT 1.5-3 times baseline.
drugs.preparationIndia: 250 mg/2.5 mL; 250 mg in 250 mL NS = 1 mg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Hepatic clearance; prolongs INR (complicates warfarin overlap).

drugs.name: Fondaparinux
drugs.adultDose: Weight < 50 kg 5 mg, 50-100 kg 7.5 mg, > 100 kg 10 mg SC once daily.

drugs.name: Methylprednisolone
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV daily for 3 days (or prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day).

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.verify: Dosing schedules vary (some use 375 mg/m² × 4 or lower fixed doses).

drugs.name: Caplacizumab
drugs.adultDose: 10 mg IV before first TPE, then 10 mg SC daily during TPE and for 30 days after.
drugs.verify: Not routinely available in India; very costly.

drugs.name: Cryoprecipitate
drugs.indications: Fibrinogen < 150 mg/dL with bleeding (< 100 in DIC without bleeding is not an indication alone)
drugs.adultDose: 1 unit/10 kg (about 8-10 units) raises fibrinogen ~50-100 mg/dL.
drugs.verify: Fibrinogen content per unit varies by blood bank.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.indications: Hyperfibrinolysis; trauma and PPH (see those modules)
drugs.adultDose: 1 g IV over 10 min, then 1 g over 8 h (trauma); in hyperfibrinolysis on viscoelastic testing 1 g IV.
